title: SkillDraft
description: An agent's proposal for a skill the fleet does not have, typically derived from external sources. Extends skill.schema.json with provenance and verification. A claim taken from the internet is a hypothesis until executed — verified_claims is what stops outdated, wrong, or hallucinated content becoming institutional knowledge. Promoted via the ordinary amendment path (docs/11 §11.8).

description.description: Must state WHEN to use this, not just what it is — it is the entire trigger (§8.5).

body.description: SKILL.md procedure. Keep short; detail goes in references.

projected_recurrence.description: Below 3, knowledge stays just-in-time and is discarded after the run. Permanent skills pay permanent context rent.

registry_checked.description: Acquisition order is registry -> project memory -> local sources -> fetch cache -> web. Drafting without checking for an existing skill is rejected at triage.

sources.description: Every claim the skill relies on must be traceable. Logged so a bad skill can be traced back to its origin.

tier.description: T3 (unknown provenance) is rejected outright and may never enter a skill. T2 is usable only with a passing verification artifact.

content_hash.description: Change means the source moved; flags the skill for re-verification.

verified_claims.description: Each load-bearing claim and the artifact proving it. 'The docs say the client retries on 429' becomes 'a scratch test confirms it against httpx==0.27.1, log attached'. C10 dissents on any draft without these.

verified_against.description: Web-sourced knowledge decays. Re-verified when this changes; failure marks the skill stale and pulls it from context packs — a stale skill is worse than a missing one, because it makes an agent confident and wrong.

eval.description: Golden tasks for this class run with and without the draft. No measured improvement, no release — cheaper to discard than to vote on.
